name: Epiq
description: Build a research database from entities, questions and source excerpts. Trace each claim to its evidence, inspect how answers changed, and export the dataset to a table or spreadsheet.

name: Conversation
description: Simulate a group discussion or focus group with EDSL agents. Set the turn order, run conversations in parallel, and analyze what participants say in response to one another.

name: Aivis
description: Track how often AI models mention or recommend a brand alongside its competitors. Repeat a set of prompts over time and measure share of voice, sentiment and citation influence.

name: Ariel
description: Split rent and assign rooms from housemates’ valuations. Check that rents add up and nobody prefers someone else’s room at its assigned price. Also allocate indivisible goods, chores, credit or shared fares.

name: Bewley
description: Code interview transcripts and other text. Build a codebook, annotate passages, write analytic memos, and export evidence tables linking themes to the words participants used.

name: Bower
description: Plan a stakeholder study around a business hypothesis. Tailor interview questions to each stakeholder, collect human or simulated responses, and trace findings to the supporting interviews.

name: Dewey
description: Conduct a literature review from a collection of papers. Follow citation trails, screen studies for inclusion, extract evidence into a matrix, and trace synthesis claims back to findings.

name: Flyvbjerg
description: Forecast from historical results for comparable projects. Build a reference class from past cases, record sources and missing observations, and use the resulting distribution as an outside view of a new estimate.

name: Green
description: Design conjoint choice tasks or best-worst surveys and export EDSL fieldwork. Estimate trade-offs, willingness to pay and preference shares from respondents’ choices. Simulate how changing an attribute affects market share.

name: Golden
description: Help a consumer compare products. Elicit preferences and constraints, collect sourced product information, then compare utility against price and see how sensitive the decision is to the inputs.

name: Helmer
description: Run a Delphi panel in repeated rounds. Collect expert estimates, return anonymous group feedback alongside each expert’s previous answer, and track consensus, revisions and disagreement.

name: Ishikawa
description: Investigate why a problem occurs. Build a fishbone diagram of candidate causes, follow chains of why questions, and track evidence and corrective actions for each explanation.

name: Kahn
description: Use two-axis scenario planning to build a matrix of four plausible futures. Turn critical uncertainties into narratives and compare how a policy or strategy performs across those futures.

name: Katz
description: Review successive versions of an academic manuscript. Anchor findings to a section and Git revision, track which concerns were resolved, and produce a review report.

name: Langley
description: Compare rival explanations using an evidence matrix. Score observations for consistency with competing hypotheses, identify contradicting evidence, and test how the ranking changes when a key observation is challenged.

name: McCall
description: Pretest job advertisements with simulated candidates. Compare variants of a posting against the same role requirements and inspect how candidate personas interpret each version.

name: MCDA
description: Rank alternatives against multiple criteria with explicit weights, thresholds and performance scores. Compare weighted-sum and ELECTRE III results and retain the judgments behind the ranking.

name: Messick
description: Pretest and validate a survey instrument. Track the construct each question should measure, revise items, and record the evidence supporting each version and its intended use.

name: Niles
description: Maintain contact records, interaction notes and follow-up tasks for a team. Connect intake surveys to relationship histories and review proposed updates before applying them.

name: Oneheart
description: Design and run Concordia social simulations. Define agent roles, treatments and outcome measurements, generate pilot code, and export results from experiments on interacting agents.

name: Premortem
description: Ask stakeholders to imagine a project has failed and explain what went wrong. Map failure modes into a causal graph, prioritize mitigations, and record open research questions.

name: Pruefung
description: Create and grade quizzes and exams with EDSL questions. Build assessments, check them before deployment, and ingest responses for grading.

name: Raiffa
description: Compare decision policies using influence diagrams, sourced probabilities and utilities. Find the thresholds where a choice changes and calculate the value of obtaining more information.

name: Roth
description: Match participants who ranked one another, such as mentors and fellows. Run deferred acceptance with either side proposing, inspect proposal histories, and check for blocking pairs and unmatched participants.

name: Spence
description: Run a hiring pipeline with EDSL application forms. Connect job posts to candidate records, track hiring stages, and collect structured reviews for candidate reports.

name: Stanton
description: Break a numerical estimate into measurable inputs. Combine sourced estimates with units, propagate uncertainty, and compare alternative calculations and their assumptions.

name: Tommy
description: Prepare simulated sales conversations, save practice attempts, and turn transcript-based feedback into coaching reports.

name: Treffen
description: Prepare a meeting by surveying and interviewing the participants. Synthesize their input into an agenda and pre-read, then preserve the decisions in a meeting record.

name: Umriss
description: Build a reusable synthetic panel that matches published population totals or percentages. Fit weights to candidate profiles against survey marginals, inspect the gaps from target distributions, and evaluate predictions on held-out items.

name: Urteil
description: Score material against a rubric using manual or model ratings. Maintain codebooks and gold standards, combine multiple raters, and rescore saved evaluations when the scorecard changes.

name: UXTest
description: Test a website with simulated users. Capture browser journeys, screenshots and traces with Playwright and EDSL, then compare findings across pages or revisions.

name: Vorhersage
description: Forecast whether an event will occur. Record evidence and probability estimates, revise them as new information arrives, then evaluate forecasts against observed outcomes.

name: Voting
description: Compare social choice rules and voting methods on the same ranked ballots. Aggregate preferences, count first choices, simulate instant-runoff elimination, and identify Condorcet winners from pairwise contests. Check how the choice of rule changes the result.

name: Zugunruhe
description: Migrate an existing Qualtrics or SurveyMonkey questionnaire to EDSL. Capture the instrument, convert it, review validation findings, and export it for use in Expected Parrot.

name: Zwicky
description: Explore a design space by combining values across dimensions. Mark incompatible combinations with cross-consistency judgments, generate feasible configurations, and compare the remaining concepts.

name: Zwill
description: Test survey digital twins against real responses and conventional baselines. Generate EDSL jobs and compare predictive performance for individuals and for the population as a whole.
